Justin Tang/The Canadian Press/AP



Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is attempting the most dramatic reorientation of his country’s economy and international alliances  since Ottawa entered a free-trade agreement with the U.S. almost 40 years ago. [https://www.wsj.com/world/europe/canada-mark-carney-european-union-a515b2a4]

On Thursday, he used an address to the European Parliament to insist that his efforts weren’t aimed at creating a third bloc “to become a great-power rival—only with better manners.”

Instead, he cast the idea of a bespoke partnership with the European Union as critical for protecting Canada’s sovereignty, at a time when it is locked in a trade war with the U.S. and confronting President Trump’s threats to make it the 51st state.

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

Planning & Investing               Rising Rates Will Make Private Equity’s Bad Year a Lot Worse

The Fed’s hike is expected to wreak havoc on funds already struggling to sell companies  and return cash to investors. [https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/rising-rates-will-make-private-equitys-bad-year-a-lot-worse-255daf59]

Market Talk               

From  Dow Jones Newswires [https://www.dowjones.com/professional/newswires/]



The Federal Reserve's rate increase will raise borrowing costs for Gulf issuers, though investor demand for regional bonds and sukuk remains resilient. Saudi banks could face particular pressure as loan growth continues to outpace deposits, making sukuk an increasingly important source of longer-term funding. Recent Saudi and Kuwaiti sukuk deals priced tighter than initial guidance, indicating demand remains healthy despite higher rates. Spreads are holding up, but overall funding costs are set to rise, potentially encouraging stronger issuers to accelerate borrowing ahead of further possible Fed increases. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

While Governor Andrew Bailey has suggested the Bank of England could raise interest rates, this would represent an insurance hike rather than concern over widening price pressures, James Smith at ING says in a note. The central bank kept rates on hold today, but signaled that future hikes could be necessary to contain rising inflation. "Still, the reality is that there's no sign that the rise in fuel and household energy bills is spilling into other parts of the inflation basket," Smith says, citing falling inflation for food as well as energy intensive good and services. He notes that policymakers calling for a hike characterized such a move as "risk management." This contrasts with the U.S. and eurozone, where rates are less clearly restrictive, he says.(don.forbes@wsj.com)

Barron's Advisor               Financial Advisers Aren’t the Only MVPs at Wealth Management Firms

Financial advisors say team members who are technically in support roles  can make a positive difference at wealth management firms. [https://www.barrons.com/advisor/articles/financial-advisors-arent-the-only-mvps-at-wealth-management-firms-7a926498?mod=advisor_center]

Business & Practice               Barrels of Sake and Rooftop Galas: Energy Traders Toast the War Boom

As geopolitical conflict disrupts global supply, commodities brokers and traders  are reaping profits. [https://www.wsj.com/business/energy-oil/barrels-of-sake-and-rooftop-galas-energy-traders-toast-the-war-boom-5b4bdb1c?mod=business_lead_story]

Impact Investing               Tokenized Stocks Get U.S. Regulator’s Green Light to Come Ashore

The SEC grants exemptions to allow venues to trade digital tokens, but give corporate issuers  the chance to block the offerings. [https://www.wsj.com/finance/regulation/tokenized-stocks-get-u-s-regulators-green-light-to-come-ashore-c37d956f]

Talking Points               The Anonymous Math Geek Who Quit Anthropic—and Became the Face of AI Safety

Long-simmering worries about the technology’s potential dangers have exploded into global consciousness  since Jacob Coxon’s dire warning. [https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/jacob-coxon-quit-anthropic-ai-safety-3f4e877c?mod=hp_lead_pos7]

Travel & Lifestyle               The 40-Minute Phone Call That Left Ed Sheeran’s Tour Hanging by a Thread            

Amanda Chen/WSJ, Getty Images (3)



Patriots owner Robert Kraft made it clear to the singer that he would cancel his tour dates at Gillette Stadium unless Macklemore was dropped from the bill.  Other NFL owners were ready to do the same. [https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/music/the-40-minute-phone-call-that-left-ed-sheerans-tour-hanging-by-a-thread-99e07984?mod=hp_lead_pos8]
